History 2008-I.subject: History
History 2008-I.question: With which one of the following did the Civil Disobedience Movement in India commerce?
options: No Tax campaign by Sardar Patel
The unfurling of the National flag by Nehru
History 2008-I.explanation: (a)  Under the leadership of Gandhiji, the Civil Disobedience Movement was launched in AD 1930. It began with the Dandi March. On 12 March 1930, Gandiji with some of his followers left the Sabarmati Ashram at Ahmedabad and made their way towards Dandi, a village on the west coast of India. Here, Gandhiji protested against the Salt Law (salt was a monopoly of the government and no one was allowed to make salt) by making salt himself and throwing up a challenge to the British government.

History 2008-I.question: Separate electorates for Muslims in India were introduced by which one of the following Acts?
History 2008-I.explanation: (a)  Government of India Act 1909 introduced separate and discriminatory electorates for Muslims. This was for the first time that, electorate for returning to the representatives to the councils was decided on the basis of class & community. For the central council, one more category Muslims was added. This was for the first time that the seats in the legislative bodies were reserved on the basis of religion for Muslims. This is called Communal representation. Sessions of Indian National Congress.

History 2008-I.subject: History
History 2008-I.question: The Treaty of Amritsar was concluded between Maharaja Ranjit Singh and who of the following?
History 2008-I.explanation: (d)  The Treaty of Amritsar of 1809 was an agreement between the British East India Company and Ranjit Singh, the Sikh leader who founded the Sikh empire. The treaty settled Indo-Sikh relations for a generation. The immediate occasion was the French threat to northwestern India, following Napoleon's Treaty of Tilsit with Russia (1807) and Ranjit Singh's attempt to bring the Cis-Sutlej states under his control. The British wanted a defensive treaty against the French and control of Punjab to the Sutlej River. Although this was not a defensive treaty, it did fix the frontier of lands controlled by Ranjit Singh broadly along the line of the Sutlej River.
